findings.title: TotalDocs iterates over b.cache without holding cacheMu
findings.body: `bleveBackend.TotalDocs` (called from `searchSupport.init` at line 216 of `pkg/storage/unified/resource/search.go`) iterates over `b.cache` without acquiring `b.cacheMu.RLock()`. Now that `BuildIndex` only locks `b.cacheMu` when writing to `b.cache` (and `getOrCreateIndex` can also trigger `BuildIndex` concurrently via watch events or search calls), reading `b.cache` without synchronization is a data race that can panic at runtime if concurrent map writes occur.

findings.title: Concurrent BuildIndex calls for the same key can race and corrupt or leak indexes
findings.body: Previously `BuildIndex` held `b.cacheMu` across the entire index creation, serializing all builds. Moving the lock to only cover `b.cache[key] = idx` means two concurrent callers for the same `NamespacedResource` (e.g. a watch event in `handleEvent` and a `Search` request both hitting `getOrCreateIndex` when the index was skipped at startup due to `initMinSize`) will both build an index concurrently. For file-backed indexes (`size > b.opts.FileThreshold`), both goroutines will call `bleve.New(dir, mapper)` on the same directory, causing one to fail or corrupt the on-disk index; for in-memory indexes, one index is silently overwritten without being closed and `IndexTenants` metrics are double-incremented.

findings.title: Cancel function and background resources are leaked if s.Init fails in NewResourceServer
findings.body: In `NewResourceServer`, `ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(...)` is created at line 229, and `s.Init(ctx)` is called at line 258. If `s.Init(ctx)` returns an error (for example, `s.initWatcher()` fails after `s.lifecycle.Init` and `s.search.init` have already started background goroutines), `NewResourceServer` returns `nil, err` without calling `cancel()` or stopping the already-initialized components, leaking the context and any background goroutines started during partial initialization.
